themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged to 5 this week versus 0.1 per week on average over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,900% spike (z-score: 14.74)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in Bed-Stuy's commercial corridors.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 14.74 indicates extreme statistical outlier
reporting_angles: Are specific blocks or corridors (e.g., near transit hubs, commercial strips) being targeted; who is posting and why now?
Has the city's enforcement or removal capacity declined, or is posting activity genuinely new?

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 52 this week versus 10.8 per week average over 8 weeks—a 384% spike (z-score: 10.86)—pointing to possible Uber/Lyft traffic congestion, illegal parking, or quality-of-service complaints.
evidence: 52 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 10.86 indicates extreme statistical outlier
reporting_angles: Are drivers clustering in specific neighborhoods (near restaurants, entertainment venues) or clogging residential streets?
Is this driven by new TLC enforcement, app-based surge pricing changes, or a spike in ride demand?

themes_detail.label: Standing Water & Flooding Risk
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints hit 3 this week compared to 0.1 per week average over 8 weeks—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—raising concerns about stormwater drainage, street flooding, or basement/foundation seepage ahead of summer weather.
evidence: 3 standing water complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical outlier
Community board has repeated DEP budget requests for environmental protection infrastructure
reporting_angles: Which blocks or intersections are affected; is this a new drainage failure or recurring seasonal issue?
Could this signal aging stormwater infrastructure or inadequate sewer capacity in Bed-Stuy's aging grid?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Spike & Homelessness Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints rose to 16 this week versus 2.6 per week average over 8 weeks—a 510% spike (z-score: 6.5)—combined with 15 homeless person assistance calls last week (224% above baseline), suggesting rapid growth in street homelessness.
evidence: 16 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (510% spike, z-score: 6.5)
15 homeless person assistance complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.6 weekly average (224% spike, z-score: 4.77)
Community board has repeated requests for DHS funding and expanded homeless services
reporting_angles: Which parks, transit stations, or public spaces have visible encampments; are they new or expanding?
Are local nonprofits and DHS overwhelmed; what support do unhoused residents lack most?

themes_detail.label: Animal Welfare Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Animal abuse complaints jumped to 9 this week versus 3.8 per week baseline—a 140% spike (z-score: 4.38)—while animal-in-park complaints spiked to 17 two weeks ago (369% above baseline), suggesting animal welfare and pest control issues.
evidence: 9 animal abuse complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.8 weekly average (140% spike, z-score: 4.38)
17 animal-in-park complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 3.6 weekly average (369% spike, z-score: 7.74)
Converging animal-related 311 signals indicate potential wildlife, rodent, or stray animal population surge
reporting_angles: Are rat populations, stray dogs, or other wildlife expanding; which parks or blocks are hotspots?
Are residents reporting abuse of animals or wildlife management conflicts; is DEC/NYPD responding?
